name: Guild socialism
summary: Guild socialism is the early twentieth-century British programme of workers' control of industry through democratic national guilds built on the trade unions, replacing the wage system and private capitalist ownership. It rejects bureaucratic state socialism, and proposes functional democracy in which producers run production while consumers, cooperatives and a communal body represent the wider public.
scope: The mainstream of the movement as systematised by G. D. H. Cole (Self-Government in Industry, Guild Socialism Restated, National Guilds League, 1915-1920s), with S. G. Hobson's National Guilds as background. Arthur Penty's medievalist, anti-factory strand is noted but excluded as a minority. Many modern issues were never addressed, so many answers are low-confidence.

sources.title: Guild socialism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of thinkers (Penty, Orage, Hobson, Cole), the state and the movement's history; also Cole's biography page for his wider outlook.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Guildsmen wanted communal provision of services with consumer representation, so public health care fits, but the sources never discuss health care and this is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Guildsmen sought to abolish the wage system itself and guarantee maintenance, not to tune a legal minimum; adherents would not clearly back or reject the reform.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Cole treats production for profit and the labour-as-commodity wage system as the evil, and sets prices through guild-cooperative negotiation toward a just price instead of free markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Guildsmen favoured nationalising railways, mines and similar industries, but only with a large measure of democratic control; the state owns while guilds run them.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Cole wants rent and surplus moved from private to communal appropriation, which implies heavy charges on wealth, though taxation rates are not discussed.

unions-good.rationale: Cole holds that trade unions are the main vehicle of change and should grow from brakes on management into bodies that take over discipline, hiring and control of industry.

property-fundamental.rationale: Guildsmen want means of production, distribution and exchange moved from private hands to communal ownership, so private property in them is not a fundamental right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The aim is to replace capitalist firms with self-governing guilds rather than regulate them, so tighter regulation is neither the goal nor opposed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Guilds would pay members continuous maintenance even in unemployment, so cutting welfare runs against the scheme, but modern welfare debates are anachronistic.

worker-ownership.rationale: Guilds give workers democratic control of industry, though formal ownership rests with the community or state; control rather than title is the point, so agreement is moderate.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Cole wants coercion minimised and personal conduct regulated as little as possible, which implies wariness of surveillance; terrorism is never addressed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Cole wants personal conduct left to public opinion rather than law, but drugs are unaddressed and Penty-style traditionalists would differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the liberty emphasis and the minimal-coercion stance pull one way while communal regulation pulls the other.

strong-leader.rationale: Cole's functional democracy spreads power and responsibility widely and attacks the omnicompetent state and bureaucracy, the opposite of a leader bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Cole criticises the omnicompetent capitalist state but keeps a Commune for civic functions, so the state is reshaped rather than called unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; Cole hopes for a part-time citizen army, which cuts against strict limits, while his minimal-coercion stance cuts the other way.

empower-police-military.rationale: Wards would appoint and control the police and the army would be a part-time citizen force, implying democratic local control rather than more authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; guildsmen left personal conduct to opinion, but adherents have no documented position.

decide-locally.rationale: Cole's Commune includes Wards that appoint and control police, and power is spread among functional and local bodies, but guilds are national so decentralisation is partial.

rehabilitation.rationale: Cole discusses courts and police structure but not penal philosophy, and the preference for minimal coercion gives only a weak lean.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; the medievalist Penty strand is traditionalist while Cole's wing is silent.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, and the period predates the issue; the liberty emphasis gives no firm answer.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by any guild socialist source, and adherents are not documented as holding a common view.

more-religion-public.rationale: Cole mentions the religious basis of medieval guilds only descriptively; he proposes cultural councils rather than a religious public role, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not an issue in guild socialist writings; the movement focused on industry.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Unaddressed in the sources; no position can be documented.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Penty's medievalism valued inherited craft culture, but Cole's wing was not nationalist; the movement is split and largely silent.

gradual-change.rationale: Cole advocates encroaching control step by step yet calls a revolutionary element unavoidable and rejects respect for established institutions as a limit, so it is genuinely split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Cole's excerpted text leaves foreign relations to the Commune and guilds and names no international body.

free-trade.rationale: Foreign trade would be handled by the guilds as organised bodies, not left to open competition, so free trade is not endorsed; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Foreign relations are barely developed and the movement is neither nationalist nor clearly internationalist.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The movement wrote about industry, not foreign military action, so no position can be derived.

open-borders.rationale: Guild writings do not discuss migration or borders; nothing in the industrial programme settles it.

limit-growth.rationale: Penty and Morris-influenced guildsmen distrusted industrial expansion for its own sake, but Cole's wing wanted efficient industry; weak inference.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Penty opposed factory production while Cole accepted modern industry; adherents split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Cole says a revolutionary element is unavoidable for thorough change and that change comes with or without violence, though coercion is a last resort.

experts-over-public.rationale: Functional democracy gives control to those doing the work and consumers a voice, not to outside experts, though teachers and professionals get self-governing roles.

central-planning.rationale: Guildsmen attack state socialism and bureaucratic control and prefer negotiation between guilds, cooperatives and the Commune over a single central plan.

socialized-markets.rationale: Guilds and the Cooperative Society negotiate prices toward a just price and guilds trade, so exchange survives under communal ownership, though not a competitive market.

land-value-tax.rationale: Cole wants rent moved to communal appropriation, but a single land tax replacing other taxes is a different scheme.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Moving rent and private appropriation to the community implies limits on inherited wealth, but inheritance is not discussed.

basic-income.rationale: Maintenance is tied to membership in a guild and service to the community, not an unconditional payment, though the guarantee is generous.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Foreign trade handled by guilds could be protective, but the sources state nothing on tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Credit and investment would be set by the Commune within limits guilds must follow, but the Commune is a functional democratic body, not the state, so it is a mixed case.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Cole permits small farms alongside guilds but wants the means of production communally owned rather than spread among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The stated aim is the abolition of the wage system, replaced by guild maintenance, but money and salaries persist in guild budgets, so only the wage-labour relation is abolished.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Cole puts credit issue, banking and currency under communal control, the opposite of leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Guilds and the cooperative society negotiate prices under the Commune, which resembles state-recognised bargaining bodies, yet Cole's guilds are democratic and run by workers rather than imposed from above.

one-party-rule.rationale: Cole's functional democracy rejects concentrated rule and the guildsmen oppose bureaucratic control, so a single leading party is contrary to the scheme.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; Cole's democratic communal constitution leaves no role for a monarch.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy is the central theme for Cole, who wants it extended into industry, though he denies parliamentary universal suffrage is real democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Cole criticises indiscriminate mass voting and wants representation by function, so direct votes on all laws are not his mode.

workers-councils.rationale: Cole puts power in functional bodies including guilds, consumer organisations and a Commune, not workers' councils alone, and parliament is reformed rather than replaced outright.

natural-rulers.rationale: Cole spreads power and responsibility widely and rejects rule by owners, implying no natural ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: Cole calls coercion a last and desperate remedy yet accepts change may come with violence and that revolution is unavoidable in part, so absolute pacifism is rejected.

war-builds-character.rationale: Cole saw war chiefly as a catalyst for worker unrest, not as ennobling; guildsmen never praise it.

separate-church-state.rationale: Church is not addressed by Cole; the medievalist strand valued religious guilds, so views vary.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Cole's Commune makes law through functional democratic bodies; scripture plays no role, though Penty's medievalism is more religious.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Cole has the Commune hold war and peace, wards appoint police and the Commune appoint judges, so these are public functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Cole hopes for a part-time citizen army under the Commune and does not aim at dominance.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not nationalist or ethnic in orientation; the movement is a class and industrial programme.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Cole uses the Marxian materialist conception to criticise democracy and sees class conflict between possessors and dispossessed, yet he is not a Marxist and stresses economic power over a class-war theory of all history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Guild budgets set salaries and the Commune sets incomes, with no firm equal-pay rule in the excerpted text.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Colonial and indigenous questions fall outside the industrial self-government programme.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Cole's sources do not take up empire or reparations, so no stance is recorded.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nothing supports this; the movement concerned industrial self-government within existing countries.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Cole contrasts commercial morality with free communal service and wants work freed from the profit motive.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cole joins freedom with a sense of serving the community but also guards personal liberty, so adherents are split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is absent from the guild texts; Morris's influence is only suggestive.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is not a guild socialist concern in the sources read.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Cole accepts modern industry and seeks to democratise it, though Penty's medievalism blamed the factory system; the mainstream disagrees.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Cole accepted modern industry while Penty resisted machinery, so the movement has no common line on disruptive technology.

human-enhancement.rationale: An anachronistic topic with no discussion in the movement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anti-bureaucratic and participatory democracy implies distrust of automated decision-making, an inference only.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; guildsmen never discussed communications privacy.

restore-past-order.rationale: Penty sought to restore the medieval gild while Cole and Hobson applied the idea to modern industry, so the movement is split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Cole argued from principles of democratic self-government rather than pragmatic results, though he favoured step-by-step methods.

direct-action.rationale: Cole describes direct action as workers using their industrial organisation to take on social functions and says political action alone cannot bring the needed economic change.

means-match-ends.rationale: Encroaching control builds workers' self-government inside the old order, so the means anticipate the guild society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Even Penty's medievalism looked to craft guilds, not foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Guilds organise production by trade and function and Cole's functionalism assumes specialised roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Guild salaries and maintenance are tied to service; the excerpted text sets out no principle of distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: The building guilds offered to produce at cost without profit, and the just price should satisfy the community's social sense.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Cole says under the wage system labour is bought as a commodity and the surplus goes to rent, interest and profit, which is a Marxian-style exploitation account.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Guildsmen reject state socialism and concentrated rule, favouring democratic functional bodies; Cole later rejected Soviet dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Cole holds that small-scale farming is compatible with socialism and farms of different sizes may coexist.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: War is treated as a catalyst of unrest, but no theory of imperialism is stated.

taxation-theft.rationale: Guildsmen want rent and surplus communally appropriated and a communal budget, so taxation is legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Cole wants personal conduct regulated as little as possible, mainly by opinion, but does not state Mill's rule.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Cole builds on functional associations and communal service, so rights are not only individual.

conscription.rationale: Cole hopes for a part-time citizen army, but conscription is not discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Cole's whole programme is extension of democratic voice into industry and politics.

state-as-business.rationale: Guildsmen explicitly oppose production for profit and the commercial treatment of labour, and reject the idea of citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Cole calls for freedom as self-government in work backed by guaranteed maintenance against unemployment.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources locate power in ownership and economic control, not in universities and media, but do not discuss them.

organic-representation.rationale: Cole argues all true and democratic representation is functional representation, through trades, consumers and local bodies rather than one parliament.

total-state.rationale: Cole attacks the omnicompetent state and bureaucratic control and divides power among guilds, consumers and communes.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not a theme of the movement.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not a theme; foreign policy is left to Commune and guilds.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The movement seeks democratic functional self-government, not oaths of loyalty, though Penty admired medieval order.

bound-labor.rationale: The guild aim is to free labour from commodity status and give workers self-government.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is not discussed in guild writings.

universal-morality.rationale: Cole contrasts commercial morality with communal service, but states no theory of universal moral truth.

single-common-good.rationale: Cole's theory separates producers and consumers as distinct interests that organise and negotiate separately rather than assume one common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism is not addressed in the guild socialist sources.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nationality and diaspora questions are absent from the movement's industrial focus.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy was no part of the guild programme.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Cole's core demand is democratic control of industry by workers, with consumers and the public having their own voice in policy.

school-vouchers.rationale: Cole sees education as a civic service run by teachers with cultural councils representing the public, not a voucher market.

economic-freedom.rationale: Cole holds economic power precedes political power and that capitalist freedom is not freedom, though liberty in self-government is cherished.

rule-by-example.rationale: No evidence of this view; Cole relies on institutions and public opinion.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not a theme of the movement.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic, since the UN did not exist; guild writings leave foreign policy to the Commune.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; Penty's strand valued religion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Immigration and welfare eligibility are not discussed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Guild maintenance goes with membership and service, but this welfare-conditionality issue is not addressed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Cole sees possessors and dispossessed as opposed classes and wants workers to take control, not partnership with employers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The medievalist and Morris-influenced strands valued inherited culture, and Cole assigns cultural councils to protect public interest.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts are outside the movement's British industrial concerns.

workers-nation.rationale: Unaddressed; guilds are national bodies but not nationalist.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The movement is not documented as supporting this; a slight inference from democratic equality.

ban-interest.rationale: Cole puts credit under communal control and moves interest to communal appropriation, but a legal ban on lending at interest is not stated.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts the democratic, egalitarian principles of the movement.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Cole reports that the majority of guildsmen see the state as an executive committee for administering the affairs of the whole capitalist class, though a minority differ.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not discussed, though Cole favoured nationalised mines under democratic control.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are not discussed in the guild sources.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in the movement.

proportional-representation.rationale: Cole opposes geographical parliamentary representation as inadequate and wants functional representation; proportional representation is not addressed.

national-mission.rationale: Not a theme of the movement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Cole says electors have little real control over representatives, but does not claim corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts equal democratic membership in the guilds.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cole's Commune controls credit, currency, defence, police and prices, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Incompatible with the movement's egalitarian democratic commitments.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Cole's functional democracy gives every worker a voice in industry, implying equal standing, though the sources do not state it as a principle.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Guildsmen aimed at national transformation and did not hold that socialism needs revolution elsewhere.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Colonialism is not discussed by guild socialists.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is not a guild socialist topic.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Cole's low-coercion stance suggests no legal restrictions on religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a concern of the guild movement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Cole treats education as a civic service but gives no view on religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Guildsmen want to reduce the state and its bureaucratic power rather than strengthen it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Cole's democratic theory demands that power rest on those governed, through functional representation.

trade-surplus.rationale: Foreign trade is handled by guilds, but no export aim is stated.

population-transfer.rationale: Incompatible with the movement's democratic and communal principles.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Cole calls coercion a bad thing and a last remedy, but he does not treat all force as wrong and accepts violent change may come.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Guild socialism replaces competitive profit-seeking with cooperative communal service and just prices.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Cole never addresses banning parties, and his minimal-coercion stance gives only a faint lean.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Cole's demand that workers not be bought as a commodity under an employer's rule matches freedom as independence from arbitrary power, though he does not use that language.

separated-powers.rationale: Cole divides power among guilds, consumer councils and a Commune with a constitutional committee and self-governing legal profession, which checks power, though not in liberal form.

vanguard-party.rationale: Guildsmen see trade union and industrial organisation of workers as the vehicle of change, not a disciplined revolutionary party.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed in the guild sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Cole wants unions to grow more powerful and take over control of industry, and uses their monopoly of labour as the lever.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Cole attributes poverty to the wage system and private appropriation of surplus.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Cole uses functional representation and election through functional bodies, and lottery is not mentioned.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Cole's minimal-coercion view implies reluctance, though emergencies are not discussed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Guilds and the cooperative society negotiate just prices, and the Commune can sell goods above or below cost for social reasons.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposed to bureaucratic and political control in industry and to concentrated power.

party-commands-army.rationale: Cole puts armed forces under the Commune, hopes for a part-time citizen army, and does not give a party command.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not discussed, though the anti-elite stance leans to agreement.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Cole distrusts representatives but does not set a rule on party discipline.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Cole places war and peace and armed forces in the Commune, not a single head of state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not addressed by Cole, and Penty's medievalism is the only religious strand.

clerical-rule.rationale: Cole's constitution rests on functional democracy, not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: War as a subject is not addressed beyond its effects on workers.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Cole wants personal conduct regulated as little as possible and cultural councils to represent the public interest.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits for presidents are not discussed; Cole's constitution has no presidency.

recall-officials.rationale: Functional democracy wants electors to control representatives more effectively, so recall fits, but recall is not discussed explicitly.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliances are not discussed; Cole leaves foreign relations to the Commune.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Rent is to be communally appropriated, not banned, and the housing question is not addressed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Cole hopes for a part-time citizen army under the Commune, which is partly in line but not a total replacement of professionals.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Penty and Morris-influenced guildsmen favoured craft and rural romance, while Cole did not stress it.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is outside the guild programme.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Cole gives teachers a special role in education and does not disparage the educated.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not discussed in the guild texts.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; Cole's minimal-coercion stance leans against but no documented position.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curricula on sexuality are not discussed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum disputes of this kind are not discussed, though Cole gives teachers self-government.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's low-regulation view of conduct is the only hint.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language rights are not part of the guild programme.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities are not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Cole wants wide individual freedom regulated by opinion, but eccentricity as a good is not stated.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Cole proposes a new constitution of Commune and guilds, but not specifically a constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Cole wants self-government and liberty in work and minimal regulation of conduct.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Development aid is not part of the guild programme.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; nuclear weapons postdate the movement's peak.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Cole's constitution has no directly elected head of state to judge.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Cole subordinates credit and currency to the communal Commune and its guild limits.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial disputes are not discussed in the movement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Guildsmen want means of production put to communal use and rent appropriated by the community, though they do not frame it as a general theory of property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Cole later admired Soviet economy but rejected dictatorship; guild sources are silent.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation doctrines are anachronistic for the movement.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees are not discussed in the sources read.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church property and clergy are not addressed by Cole.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Heads of state are not part of the guild constitution.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is not addressed in guild socialist sources.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special regional status is not addressed, though Cole favours functional and ward autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contradicts the democratic constitution of Cole's Commune.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Wealth is to be communally appropriated; a flat tax matches nothing in guild thinking.

character-from-environment.rationale: Cole's emphasis on the wage system, freedom in work and environment shaping people is consistent with this but not stated as such.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Cole sets a constitutional committee and self-governing legal structures to hold bodies to law.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; space is not a topic for the movement.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Cole's constitution mixes functional bodies and a Commune, but not rule of the few and the many in the classical sense.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist question concerns party states and not the guild model.

land-redistribution.rationale: Cole wants rent communally appropriated and allows small farms, but does not call for splitting estates among farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugees and conflict returns are not discussed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not part of the movement and nationalist claims are alien to it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contradicts the minimal regulation of personal conduct.

common-currency.rationale: Currency would be communal and national in Cole's scheme; the idea is unaddressed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnic union across borders is not part of the movement.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Unaddressed, though functional autonomy is the movement's theme.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration and homelands are not discussed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cole applies the Marxian materialist conception of history, saying economic power precedes political power, though he is not strictly Marxist.

ban-cartels.rationale: Unaddressed; guilds themselves are monopolistic bodies.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed; the guild scheme replaces capitalist firms and credit rather than rescuing them.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Cole's constitution has a constitutional committee and self-governing legal profession, so courts are not simply bound.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not discussed in guild writings.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is not part of the guild programme.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements are not discussed beyond guilds handling foreign trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: Cole's free communal service ideal ties work to social duty, but a formal programme of replacing material incentives is not stated.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Cole sees industrial action by union organisation as the lever and treats sudden seizure of power as very difficult.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Cole's removal of private rent and surplus and democratic functional control implies ending hereditary privilege, though not stated.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not stated; democratic self-government principles suggest rejection.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotic schooling is not discussed; Cole treats education as a civic service run with teachers.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race preferences are anachronistic for the movement.

public-money-creation.rationale: Cole places credit issue, banking and currency under communal control.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Cole sees war and workers' unrest weakening capitalism and expects replacement via encroaching control.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial legacy influence is not discussed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Imperialism theory is not part of guild socialism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contradicts the egalitarian and communal principles.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Cole has a constitutional committee but no bill of rights is discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Democratic functional representation is elective, though the statement is about the political nation.

minority-veto.rationale: Cole's constitution has binding decisions of bodies and a last-resort coercion, and does not give individuals vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Cole does not discuss the resistance rights of subjects to a ruler.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Cole rejects the omnicompetent Parliament and wants its sovereignty replaced by functional bodies.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Guildsmen want rights and control for workers, not paternal duty of the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Cole requires active participation by workers in self-government.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Cultural critique of mass media is not part of the guild texts.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Cole stresses economic power and hunger and fear as past means of control, but not hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is outside the movement.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nativist office rules are not discussed.

party-own-road.rationale: The guild movement had no international party line to deviate from.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic for the 1910s; Cole later opposed fascism but this is not guild socialism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic for the movement's 1910s peak, and Cole's later views are separate.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is not discussed by guild socialists.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Public monuments and commemoration are not discussed by the movement.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's disadvantage programmes are not discussed by guild writers.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence services are not discussed in guild sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The question of cultural suitability of institutions is not discussed.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Cole puts the army under the civil Commune.

paid-care-work.rationale: Domestic labour is not discussed in the guild sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Cole uses functional election and appointment by bodies, with no mention of civil service examinations.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Cole wants real control by electors over their representatives, in line with this, but recall is not described.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Guild maintenance is collective and communal, so private savings accounts do not fit.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Cole wants communal appropriation of rent but allows small farms, so adherents would not hold use-only tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Cole rejects parliament as it is, but the Commune controls budgets, so a functional analogue exists.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not part of the programme.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership of land is not discussed, though rent is to be communal.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Morris-influenced guildsmen criticised commercial morality, but the statement is not directly addressed.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is not discussed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: No documented position; democratic principles suggest rejection.

corporate-influence.rationale: Cole's argument that economic power precedes political power implies capital shapes politics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Funding of NGOs and universities is not discussed in guild writings.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are not discussed, though wards have local authority.

job-guarantee.rationale: Guilds would provide continuous maintenance protecting workers from unemployment, which is close to a job or income guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: International relations theory is not discussed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Cole keeps a Commune with law, though coercion is minimised.

non-intervention.rationale: Not discussed in the sources read.

industrial-unions.rationale: Guildsmen want unions that control an industry as a whole, with national guilds by industry replacing craft separation.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in the movement.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Cole's participatory emphasis suggests openness, but freedom of information was not discussed.

local-production.rationale: Penty's craft revival leans that way but Cole's national guilds do not.

informal-organisation.rationale: Cole builds permanent unions, guilds and a Commune, not small informal groups.

religious-nation.rationale: Not part of Cole's programme, though Penty's strand is religious.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary diplomacy is far from the movement.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Cole wants personal conduct and property regulated as little as possible while the means of production go communal.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anachronistic; Cole later rejected Soviet dictatorship but did not call for defeating communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Cole has guilds and cooperatives serving consumers under communal oversight but not private providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Cole mentions religion respectfully in the medieval gild context and not as an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Cole sees modern industry as the base for guilds, but capitalism as exploitative, so he is split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's equality is not addressed in the guild writings.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not part of the guild programme.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cole uses cooperative organisations and Wards, but not small communes holding property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: No documented position; alien to the movement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Guildsmen reject both state socialism and capitalism and propose guilds as a third path, though they borrow from Marx.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Competing historical land claims are not discussed by guild writers.

holocaust-denial.rationale: A factual denial with no basis in the movement; the statement is not about guild socialism, so inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Cole wants conduct regulated as little as possible, but the issue is not addressed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Opposed to bureaucratic control and concentrated power; Cole wants coercion minimal.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Cole's low-coercion stance and secular constitution imply rejection.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not part of the movement; colonial questions are unaddressed.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious doctrine outside the movement's scope.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Cole argues democracy must reach into industry and that workers need direct rights to frame rules and choose leaders in their workplaces.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Guild socialism identified itself on the left and set itself between state socialism and capitalism, so obsolescence is not endorsed.

alienated-labor.rationale: Cole's critique of labour as a bought commodity under the wage system and call for freedom in work echo alienation, though without that term.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Cole's authority comes from functional democratic bodies; Penty's medievalism is more religious.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not discussed by guild writers.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace law of this type is anachronistic for the movement.

social-market-economy.rationale: Cole replaces capitalist ownership with guilds and communal control, going beyond social protection of a market economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Cole expects the Commune to direct armed forces, hoping for a citizen army.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian aims suggest rejection.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Cole's communal credit system is non-profit and communal, but user-owned banks are not specified.

property-franchise.rationale: Cole demands wider democratic power, not property qualifications.

reification.rationale: Cole's critique of labour as a commodity is akin to this but not stated in these terms.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Cole's premise that economic power precedes political power implies this, though press ownership is not discussed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Cole sets out courts and constitutional law but doesn't state this principle.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; internet deliberation is outside the sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Cole explains inequality through the wage system and economic power, and nothing in guild socialism endorses racial hereditarianism; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Cole has wards control police and the Commune direct forces, which suggests accountability, but past abuses are not discussed.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement never made this claim and its democratic communal outlook implies disagreement, but it did not address diversity.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation and occupation are not addressed by the guild writers.

delink-world-market.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not discussed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Guilds would handle foreign trade and the Commune credit, which implies public control of strategic industry, but takeovers are not discussed.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Cole held that representation should be functional, by trade and interest, rather than by one body chosen at large, so a random general assembly cuts against it; inferred from this view.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Guildsmen were mostly secular reformers who wanted institutions adapted to modern conditions, but the sources never discuss religious doctrine and this is inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Cole treats concentrated capitalist ownership and the wage system as the root of industrial servitude and wants power over industry spread to workers' guilds.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Guildsmen were liberal-left on personal liberty, but the sources never discuss sexuality; inferred from their general democratic principles.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Guild socialism rejected state sovereignty over social life and favoured a plural society, so a state-run atheist curriculum is inferred to be unwelcome; the sources are silent.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Cole's communal body keeps coercive functions and the sources never propose abolishing police or prisons; inferred from his reformist institutional design.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Cole's pluralism divides sovereignty among guilds, cooperatives and a communal body rather than one majority; extended by inference to divided communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Guildsmen wanted maintenance guaranteed as a right through the abolition of the wage system and communal provision, not left to charity.

term-limits.rationale: Cole wanted elected, recallable officials but never addressed term limits; adherents have no clear stance.

vote-delegation.rationale: Functional representation, with delegates answerable on each function and subject to recall, is close to topic-by-topic delegation, though Cole never proposed vote transfer; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The question is anachronistic and the sources never address it; nothing in the principles points either way.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Guild socialists of the period generally backed women's equality, but the sources never discuss religious office; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Guild socialism sought democratic equality in social life and many adherents supported women's emancipation; marriage itself is not discussed, so this is inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Cole stressed functional representation more than residence, and no stance on foreign residents is recorded; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Cole expected communal bodies to provide public services and regulate prices (s2), so rent regulation fits; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: The sources do not address patents and copyrights; guildsmen wanted producer control, not abolition of IP.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Cole was anti-militarist and sought workers' self-government (s1), so drilled youth organisations for national service are disfavoured; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Guildsmen were generally anti-militarist and Cole opposed war, so nuclear arms would be rejected; the issue postdates the movement and is inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Cole's internationalist socialism opposed military blocs (s2); the issue was never discussed, so inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The movement did not address genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The programme is the abolition of the wage system and of capitalist ownership, with industry run by those who work in it (s1, s2).

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Cole's discussion of coercion and police (s2) accepts limited force, so an absolute ban would be rejected; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Guildsmen based politics on function and workplace, not national identity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Sex was not a topic for guildsmen, and the era's view treated sex as biological; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Guildsmen did not address feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Guildsmen were secular and anti-militarist, so a cult of national martyrs is unlikely; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Cole's politics was about industrial democracy, not spiritual struggle; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Guildsmen placed social reorganisation of industry first; the medievalist Penty strand aside, no cultural-first claim; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Guildsmen took no stand on religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The sources do not address religion and women.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Guildsmen's functional democracy gives control to all producers regardless of origin (s1, s2); inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Cole favoured regional communes organised by function and locality, not by people; the topic is not addressed.

independent-unions.rationale: Guilds are built on democratically run trade unions that Cole wants kept free of bureaucratic state control.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Workers' control of industry through democratic guilds is the movement's core demand, on the basis that producers must rule production.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Cole gave consumers and a communal body a voice in services; inferred that essentials stay communal.

second-chamber.rationale: Cole's functional democracy proposed a communal body beside a guild congress, so more than one representative chamber; low confidence.

municipal-property.rationale: Cole has guilds run industry, with the state holding nominal ownership, rather than local communities owning it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Cole favoured both local communes and national guilds, but the sources do not describe municipal confederations.

family-wage.rationale: The guildsmen demanded a guaranteed maintenance in place of the wage system; inferred that pay should support a family.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Cole opposed state domination of the individual and valued self-government, so the person comes first; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement was largely secular but had a medievalist strand; sources do not settle it.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The sources do not describe the powers of regions.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Guild socialism is organised by industry and class function, not race; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; the movement focused on class and function.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Many guildsmen opposed militarism and the First World War; inferred, low confidence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Cole's functional democracy and internationalism rest on producers and consumers, not language or nation; inferred as the sources do not address it.

communal-electorates.rationale: Guildsmen proposed representation by function (trade and consumer bodies), not by religious community; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Guild socialism blamed capitalism and the capitalist state for conflict rather than foreign plots; inferred from its internationalist labour outlook.

free-public-college.rationale: Guildsmen wanted communal provision of services and an educated producing class; free higher education is inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation was never discussed; no position follows from the principles.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from Cole's picture of industry and land held in trust by a commune for the community as a whole rather than for private gain.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Guildsmen sought women's equality but did not claim a distinct female perspective; the sources do not address it.

arms-reduction.rationale: Guild socialism opposed capitalist militarism, and Cole's treatment of defence in the sources treats armed force as a limited function; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: British socialists of the period opposed secret treaties; inferred for the Guild movement, whose sources never discuss diplomacy directly.

capital-controls.rationale: Cole's guild scheme places credit and currency under public control; controlling capital flows is inferred from that.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Cole's scheme leaves defence and police to a communal body representing citizens, which implies state monopoly, but the sources treat this only briefly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Guildsmen were largely anti-militarist and Cole was a conscientious objector, but the movement made no doctrine of soldiers' refusal; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Guilds were to be built on the trade unions, which set pay and conditions collectively; the programme rests on organised industrial bodies, not individual contracts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Guildsmen aimed to abolish the wage system rather than top it up through the state; inferred, as the issue is anachronistic.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Cole wanted credit and currency under public control for social ends, so fixed legal borrowing limits are unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Cole was internationalist and wanted cooperation among guilds across countries, but never addressed development rules; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Cole's strategy was encroaching control from within and a Commune that reshapes rather than abolishes the state, not a revolutionary smashing of it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Guild socialism had a fixed guild blueprint but allowed cooperatives and consumer bodies alongside guilds; adherents' view of pluralism is not stated.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's focus was industrial control and not valuation of nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Cole's functional democracy treats the nation-state as one association among many, not a sacred community; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Guildsmen wanted education publicly provided and free of financial burden; student loans are anachronistic and this is inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, whose analysis was of class and industry.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; the sources give no view on human nature as basis of rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Cole wanted the press and culture free of both capitalist and bureaucratic control, which fits independent public media; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The guild programme was about industrial organisation and never addressed whether religions share one truth, so adherents are indifferent.

farm-price-support.rationale: Cole's scheme included agricultural guilds and cooperative organisation with consumer representation, so state or cooperative support for farmers is inferred from its anti-market, communal outlook.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement; inferred from its hostility to state coercion and Cole's later Labour-left pacifist leanings, adherents would lean against keeping them.

workers-own-party.rationale: Guildsmen put industrial organisation through the unions ahead of parliamentary politics and were sceptical of the state, so a separate workers' party was not their main route.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; a ban follows from the movement's general egalitarian, communal-welfare outlook and is inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; equal legal property rights for women is inferred from the movement's egalitarian democracy and its call for equal industrial citizenship.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language naming was outside the movement's concerns, so it is genuinely indifferent.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Cole wanted industry and public services run by guilds and a communal body answerable to all affected, not private suits between property owners, so agency or communal regulation is inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Cole's functional democracy represents people by trade and as consumers, not by hereditary custom, so a formal role for chiefs does not fit; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmentalism was not addressed; Penty's anti-industrial strand would agree but the Cole mainstream would not, so adherents split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Cole's criticism of coercive state machinery and preference for self-government, which favours discretion over rigid rules.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The movement never discussed immigration or language policy, and its internationalist and communal strands point in different directions.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Guild socialism made the trade unions the basis of the guilds with all workers in an industry belonging, so membership could not be optional; Cole does not discuss modern right-to-work rules.

voter-id.rationale: Not discussed; guildsmen cared about functional representation rather than ballot procedure.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The sources never address it and guildsmen did not agree on religion; treated as split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The sources never address it; inferred from the movement's pluralist view of the state as one association among many.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Cole held that democracy needs real self-government in every association, including industry, and criticised parliamentary voting alone as unrepresentative.

premarital-sex.rationale: The sources do not discuss sexual morality; inferred from the movement's secular, reforming, libertarian socialist outlook.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's hostility to bureaucratic state power and its stress on self-government.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Guildsmen wanted the wage system abolished and communal provision and guaranteed maintenance through the guilds, not a state cash payment; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Cole's democratic socialism required equal citizenship and the movement flourished alongside the suffrage campaign, but the sources do not state it directly.

race-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's egalitarian socialism, since the sources do not discuss race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Guildsmen distrusted central bureaucracy yet wanted communal bodies to provide services; no source covers it, so this is treated as split.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Cole's view that industry and its resources should be held in common and run by guilds, not by individual first claimants.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Cole's internationalism and anti-war stance; international criminal courts did not exist in his period.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secular, rationalist character; Cole's texts do not discuss scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic egalitarianism and support for women's equality; not discussed for Indigenous self-rule.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Cole opposed bureaucratic state socialism and wanted workers' control of industry instead of state management.

indirect-election.rationale: Cole's functional democracy builds representation upward through guild and regional bodies chosen by delegates, rather than one direct vote on everything.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secular and egalitarian outlook; the question is not discussed.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from Cole's federal, decentralised model of self-government with many self-governing communities.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on democratic self-government; the question is not discussed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; Cole's decentralism and anti-imperialism pull in different directions, so no clear inference.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Cole's aim of abundant production for all under workers' control, though Penty's medievalist strand, excluded here, favoured simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the movement and no clear inference from its principles.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was largely anti-militarist but took no clear position on drafting women.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Guild socialism was an internationalist, class-based programme; the sources never discuss a spiritual bond with the homeland, so this is inferred from its focus on producers' self-government.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Cole's functional democracy rests on communal self-government and consent rather than coercion; the sources never address extrajudicial killing, so this is inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: The movement predates modern China relations and its sources never discuss them; nothing in its principles favours either option.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Cole's guild socialism had no nationalist programme of this kind, so support for kin minorities abroad is inferred to be unfavoured.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Cole's Commune and guild system put land and natural resources under communal or guild ownership instead of private appropriation, which fits common ownership though compensation is not discussed.

self-ownership.rationale: Cole's attack on wage slavery implies each worker's rights over their own labour, but the sources do not discuss self-ownership by name; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Guildsmen discussed credit, prices and currency but not consumption taxes; adherents have no clear position.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Guildsmen wanted communal provision of services for all citizens through consumer representation rather than poor-only relief, inferred from their functional democracy.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Guild Socialism Restated builds representation on functional bodies such as guilds, consumers' councils and the Commune, not on bypassing associations for a leader, so the claim runs against the core scheme.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Cole attacked the privileged position of capitalist owners; the statement is not discussed directly, so this is inferred from his opposition to capitalist privilege.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Guild socialism's politics was organised by function (producers, consumers), not faith; this is inferred as the sources never address denominations.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Cole embraced industrial production under workers' control; the medievalist return to the past was Penty's excluded minority view, so adherents mostly decline the combination. Inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Cole's circle was progressive on women's equality, but divorce law is not discussed in the sources; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: National guilds would control industries on behalf of the community, so resources under national rather than foreign control fits; the sources do not discuss foreign ownership, so this is inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Cole's case for abolishing the wage system and capitalist ownership judges distribution by the social equality of producers rather than by how holdings arose; inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Cole's work on credit and currency suggests community control of finance, but the tax is a later proposal; inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The question is anachronistic for a 1910s-20s British movement focused on industry and class, and adherents have no recorded position.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Cole argued the state has no absolute claim on obedience and that individuals owe loyalty to just functional bodies, which fits this, though natural-law wording is not used; inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Guildsmen wanted to end drudgery and release time for self-government and leisure, but automation is not discussed; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: The sources do not address world order; guildsmen favoured international cooperation of producers, not clearly for or against multipolarity.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Cole drew on Marx and held that labour produces wealth and should not be treated as a commodity, but the sources do not state the value theory itself; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Guild socialism was internationalist and focused on producers' control, so a link to patriotism is inferred as unfavoured.

material-over-identity.rationale: Cole's programme centred on workers' control of industry and the wage system, which fits a focus on material interests; cultural identity politics did not exist, so inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Cole rejected state socialism and bureaucratic control, and wanted workers' guilds rather than a party to run industry, so party leadership of a market economy runs against the programme.

missingStatements.text: Consumers, as well as producers, should have an organised voice in running each industry.
missingStatements.rationale: Cole holds that producers control internal management while organised consumers, chiefly cooperatives, represent the public interest in quality, price and policy.

missingStatements.text: Decisions on social questions should be made by bodies representing people according to their function, such as their trade, rather than by one geographically elected parliament.
missingStatements.rationale: Cole argues that all true and democratic representation is functional representation, since a single representative cannot speak for a person on every question.

missingStatements.text: Workers should gradually take control of their industry from within, step by step, before capitalist owners are dispossessed.
missingStatements.rationale: Cole's strategy of encroaching control has unions take over discipline, hiring and supervision inside the existing system.

notes: Cole's wing and Penty's medievalist wing differ on religion, machinery and the state; Cole's majority view is used. The majority of the National Guilds League saw the state as a capitalist instrument, while a minority thought it could be adapted. Britannica could not be opened and was not cited.
